explain.title: Biology studies life
explain.body: Biology is the science of life. The word comes from the Greek words bios (life) and logos (study). It explores the structures, functions, and interactions of living organisms.

explain.title: The three major fields
explain.body: Zoology: It is the study of animals, including their structure, function, behaviour, and diversity. Botany: It is the study of plants, including their structure, growth, reproduction, and interactions with their environment. Microbiology: The study of microorganisms, such as bacteria and microscopic fungi is called microbiology. It includes the study of the structures, functions, habitats and reproduction of microorganisms, and their impacts on health and environment.

explain.title: Form, structure, and function
explain.body: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms. Anatomy is the branch of Biology that explores the internal physical structure of organisms, particularly humans. Physiology is the branch of Biology that deals with the functioning of body parts.

explain.title: Tissues, cells, and molecules
explain.body: Histology is the microscopic study of tissues. Cytology is the study of cells i.e., the building blocks of life. Molecular Biology deals with the study of biological molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.

explain.title: Development, inheritance, fossils, and classification
explain.body: Embryology is the study of the process of development of organism from fertilized egg. Genetics is the branch of Biology that deals with the study of transfer of characteristics from parents to offspring. Palaeontology is the branch of Biology that deals with the study of fossils. Taxonomy is the branch of Biology that deals with the classification of organisms into groups on the basis of similarities and differences.

explain.title: Organisms, environments, and health
explain.body: Ecology is the branch of Biology that deals with the relationships between organisms and their environment. Marine Biology is the branch of Biology that deals with the study of life in oceans. Pathology is the study of diseases, their causes, and effects. Immunology is the branch in which we study the components of the immune system and their role against diseases. Pharmacology is the branch in which we study drugs and their effects on the body.

mistakes: Do not confuse Anatomy, which studies internal physical structure, with Physiology, which studies how body parts function.
Do not confuse Histology, the study of tissues, with Cytology, the study of cells.
Do not mix up Zoology (animals), Botany (plants), and Microbiology (microorganisms).
For a branch definition, write what it studies rather than only giving an example.

explain.title: Biochemistry and Biophysics
explain.body: Biochemistry is the study of the structure and reactions of different chemical substances present in living systems. Biophysics applies principles of Physics to biological processes; for example, rules of lever and motion help us understand muscles, bones and joints.

writtenQuestions.text: How can a scientist apply the scientific method to confirm an observation that a certain plant species grows more quickly in shady places than in direct sunlight?
modelAnswer: Recognize the problem: Does this plant species grow more quickly in shady places than in direct sunlight?
Observe and measure the growth of similar plants in shady places and direct sunlight.
Hypothesis: This plant species grows more quickly in shady places than in direct sunlight.
Deduction: If the hypothesis is true, then plants grown in shade will show more growth than similar plants grown in direct sunlight.
Grow similar plants in the two light conditions, keeping other factors the same, and measure their growth over the same period.
Use the results to decide whether the observations support the hypothesis.

explain.title: The scientific method
explain.body: Scientists take specific steps for doing scientific work or research. These steps are called the scientific method. Learn the six steps in order: recognition of a scientific problem, observation, hypothesis, deduction, experiments, and results.

explain.title: Observations
explain.body: “Qualitative observations involve observations that cannot be measured with numbers.” “Quantitative observations involve measurements or numerical data that can be expressed in terms of quantity.” For example, flower colour is qualitative, while the number of birds in a tree is quantitative.

explain.title: Hypothesis
explain.body: “Such tentative answer of scientific problem is called hypothesis.” A hypothesis is a proposed answer that matches available observations, can be tested through experiments, and can be disproved.

explain.title: Deduction and experiments
explain.body: “Such logical results of hypotheses are called deductions.” Deductions often use an if-then pattern: if a hypothesis is true, then a particular result should happen. Experiments test hypotheses; a control group provides a comparison with the experimental group.

explain.title: Results
explain.body: Scientists gather data from experiments and use statistical analyses and graphs to summarize results. They report and share findings with other scientists.

mistakes: Leaving out a step or putting deduction before hypothesis; learn the six steps in order.
Calling an observation a hypothesis. An observation is information gathered; a hypothesis is a tentative answer to the problem.
Confusing a deduction with a hypothesis. A deduction predicts what should happen if the hypothesis is true.
Calling a non-numerical observation quantitative. Quantitative observations use measurements or numerical data.
Saying that a hypothesis is always correct. It must be tested and there must be a way to disprove it.
Describing an experiment without identifying the comparison between experimental and control groups.

explain.title: Biology has many branches
explain.body: Biology covers many kinds of living organisms and processes. Branches such as Botany, Zoology, and Microbiology make the subject easier to organise and study. Other branches focus on a particular feature, such as cells, tissues, functions, development, or classification.

explain.title: Branches focus on different questions
explain.body: Genetics studies heredity and variation; Anatomy studies structure; and Physiology studies functions. Morphology is concerned with form and external features. Taxonomy deals with classification, while Embryology studies development from fertilization.

explain.title: Biology connects with other subjects
explain.body: Biology works with Physics, Chemistry, Statistics, Geography, Economics, and Computer Science. For example, Biochemistry studies chemical processes in living organisms, while Computational Biology uses computers to work with biological data.

explain.title: Scientific investigation follows ordered steps
explain.body: A scientist begins with observations, proposes a hypothesis, makes deductions, and tests them with experiments. Results are then analysed. Evidence may support a hypothesis, show that it should be rejected, or lead to its modification.

explain.title: Scientific knowledge is shared and tested
explain.body: Scientists share observations and results and build on earlier work. The investigation of malaria shows how different contributions about the parasite and mosquitoes helped explain how the disease spreads.

notes.answer: Biology is the science of life. Its major fields are Zoology, Botany, and Microbiology, and its sub-fields focus on particular structures, processes, organisms, or relationships.

notes.simple: Different sciences help us study different parts of life: its chemicals, movement, data, locations, useful products and economic value.

notes.answer: Science is collaborative when researchers from different disciplines work together to solve complex problems.
notes.explanation: Scientists from different fields can combine their knowledge and skills to investigate problems that are too complex for one field alone. For example, cancer research may involve biologists, geneticists, pharmacologists and statisticians.

notes.title: Scientific Method
notes.answer: The scientific method is the ordered process used to investigate a scientific problem: recognition of a problem, observation, hypothesis, deduction, experiments, and results.
notes.explanation: The scientific method is a set of steps scientists use to investigate a problem. They make observations, suggest a testable hypothesis, work out what should happen if it is true, test it with experiments, and report the results.
notes.simple: A scientist asks a question, makes a possible explanation, tests it fairly, and shares what happened.
steps: Recognize and define the scientific problem.
Make observations and study previous research.
Propose a hypothesis that matches the observations and can be tested.
Make a deduction: predict what should happen if the hypothesis is true.
Perform experiments to test the hypothesis.
Collect and summarize results, then share the findings.

notes.title: From Hypothesis to Theory and Law
notes.answer: A theory that is proved again and again by experiments becomes a law or principle.
notes.explanation: A hypothesis that is supported by experiments can lead to a theory. Scientists continue to test theories, and a theory proved repeatedly by experiments becomes a law or principle.
notes.simple: Test an idea, test it again, and use the results to build scientific explanations.
examples: The theory of evolution explains how species change over time through natural selection.
Hardy-Weinberg law and Mendel’s laws of inheritance are examples of biological laws.
steps: Experiments prove a hypothesis correct.
Scientists use the supported hypothesis to make further hypotheses.
When the new hypotheses are also proved, the original hypothesis becomes a theory.
Scientists keep testing the theory and try to disprove it.
If experiments prove it again and again, it becomes a law or principle.

notes.title: Branches of Biology and the Scientific Method
notes.answer: Biology is the study of life, and the scientific method uses observations, hypotheses, deductions, and experiments to investigate biological questions.
notes.explanation: Biology is the study of life. It has many branches because living things can be studied in different ways: by their structure, functions, development, relationships, and classification. Scientists use observations, hypotheses, deductions, and experiments to investigate questions.
notes.simple: Biology studies living things. Its branches help us focus on one kind of question at a time. The scientific method is a careful way to test possible answers.
examples: Physiology studies the functions of living organisms and their parts.
steps: Observe a problem or pattern.
Form a hypothesis that could explain it.
Make deductions from the hypothesis.
Test the deductions with experiments.
Analyse the results and decide whether the hypothesis is supported.
